Why: The default export is imported without braces, under any name you choose. Named exports go in braces and must match the exported name.

Docs: MDN — JavaScript modules — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Modules
quote: Each module can have up to one default export.

back:
SyntaxError: The requested module './math.js' does not provide an export named 'add'

Why: add is the default export, not a named one. Imports are checked before any code runs, so nothing is printed. Write `import add from "./math.js"`.

Docs: MDN — import — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/import
quote: The static import declaration is used to import read-only live bindings which are exported by another module.

Docs: MDN — import — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/import
quote: The imported bindings are called live bindings because they are updated by the module that exported the binding, but cannot be re-assigned by the importing module.
